note: Inputs of the rules-fix-v1 build. Each task is a merged upstream bug fix with a linked issue: base is the fix commit's parent, src_files and test_files are what the fix changed, the hidden tests are the test_*.py files among test_files, expect holds the oracle's test counts, and wrong is a plausible wrong fix (exact text replacements on the fix's or the base's files, per wrong_from). fetch-sources.ts vendors the trees and issue texts and fills in stripped and the sha256 fields; build.ts reads only the vendored files.

wrong.replace: dot_idx = idx if dot_idx is None else dot_idx

tasks.wrong_why: takes the first dot instead of the last, so a.b.c still names b.
treats BEGIN TRANSACTION as a statement but still counts newlines before BEGIN as content.
makes NULLS FIRST/LAST an order keyword but does not join it with a preceding ASC or DESC.
copies the table highlight setting only once the table already has rows.
reads a missing field as None instead of leaving it out, so the repr shows item=None.
strips control codes only from tokens that have no style.

wrong.replace: elif default_value is not None and default_value == "":

tasks.wrong_why: still compares the default with an empty string first, which raises for types that refuse the comparison.

wrong.find: self._flag_needs_value = flag_value is not UNSET or self.default is UNSET
wrong.replace: self._flag_needs_value = flag_value is not UNSET and self.default is UNSET

tasks.wrong_why: requires both flag_value and a missing default before the value becomes optional.
turns non-string choices into strings but still lists every choice when show_choices is off.
drops extra labels but no longer pads missing labels with empty strings.
moves the defaults after the base constructor but keeps the base missing-value check, so required=True still fails.

wrong.find: self.schemes = {s.lower() for s in schemes} if schemes else self.default_schemes
wrong.replace: self.schemes = set(schemes) if schemes else self.default_schemes

tasks.wrong_why: stores the custom schemes as a set without lowercasing them.
handles n == 0 but lets a negative n through to islice.
stops the lookup from creating keys but never records keys whose items went straight to the caller.
calls iter() explicitly but still inside the try, so the TypeError is still swallowed.
adds target-aware forwarding but never passes the wrapped target to it.
adds __getstate__ and __setstate__ but not __new__, so unpickling sets items before the linked list exists.
escapes the pipe character in header rows only.

wrong.find: num_cols = len(list_of_lists[0]) if list_of_lists else len(headers)

tasks.wrong_why: treats an empty table as having no columns, so the header widths list does not match the headers.
adds __copy__ but not __deepcopy__.
also catches KeyError from the choice function, but a custom choice function can raise anything.

wrong.replace: if obj is None and self.__attrname is None:

tasks.wrong_why: skips the instance-dict rewrite for class access only when the method has no attribute name.
drops the old expiry entry but leaves the old value in the cache.
checks the private ranges whatever the flag says, but still returns False for a public address when private=False.

wrong.find: fragment = fragment.lstrip("/") if fragment.startswith("/") else fragment

tasks.wrong_why: strips trailing slashes from the fragment instead of leading ones.
makes escape optional but never applies it to a renderer instance that was passed in.
stops escaping inline code in the parser but does not escape it in the HTML renderer.

wrong.replace: if type(maxcolwidths) is tuple and len(maxcolwidths) == 1:

tasks.wrong_why: converts a tuple only when it has a single width.

wrong.find:
elif valtype is int:
        return format(val, intfmt)

tasks.wrong_why: skips the format for integer strings, so plain ones work but colored ones are left unformatted.
recognises IF NOT EXISTS as one keyword but not IF EXISTS.

wrong.find: if self.show_envvar and self.envvar is not None:
wrong.replace: if self.show_envvar and ctx.auto_envvar_prefix is None:

tasks.wrong_why: hides the hint only when an auto env var prefix is set, not when the option has no env var.
matches the scheme case-insensitively but still only rewrites a lowercase file:/// prefix.
gets an iterator to test for scalars but then calls iter() on the object again.
copies every attribute from the async function, so the wrapper no longer points back at the sync filter.
converts only the destination parts to a list, so a tuple of base parts plus a list still fails.
passes markup=None, which still falls back to the console setting.
